config_fields.name: task
config_fields.description: The specific task to perform using the skill. Becomes the user turn in LLM mode.

config_fields.name: execution_mode
config_fields.description: How to execute the skill

config_fields.name: input_mapping
config_fields.description: Maps descriptive input names to CARL context refs. Keys are interpolated into the task string via {key} placeholders. Values use CARL reference syntax ($history[-1], $memory.ns.key, etc.)

config_fields.name: output_key
config_fields.description: Key label for result in history entry

config_fields.name: output_memory_key
config_fields.description: If set, write the skill's text result to this memory key under the 'agent_skill' namespace. Useful for wiring parallel skill branches: each branch writes to a different key, and a downstream step reads them all via $memory.agent_skill.<key>.

config_fields.name: output_memory_namespace
config_fields.description: Memory namespace for output_memory_key writes (default: 'agent_skill').

config_fields.name: output_file_key
config_fields.description: If set, write the path of any output file produced by the skill to memory key 'agent_skill.<output_file_key>'

config_fields.name: llm_config
config_fields.description: Optional LLM config override (model, temperature, max_tokens). Uses context default if None.

nested_fields.name: model
nested_fields.description: Model identifier to use for this step (e.g., 'openai/gpt-4o', 'anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet')

nested_fields.name: temperature
nested_fields.description: Temperature for this step (overrides default)

nested_fields.name: max_tokens
nested_fields.description: Max tokens for this step (overrides default)

nested_fields.name: timeout
nested_fields.description: Timeout for this step in seconds (None = use chain default)

nested_fields.name: token_budget_warning
nested_fields.description: Emit a warning when total tokens consumed by this step exceed this threshold. None = no warning. Only works with clients that return usage info (e.g. OpenAICompatibleClient).

nested_fields.name: execution_mode
nested_fields.description: Execution strategy for this step

nested_fields.name: self_critic_evaluators
nested_fields.description: Ordered evaluator names for SELF_CRITIC mode; all must approve

nested_fields.name: self_critic_max_revisions
nested_fields.description: Maximum candidate regeneration rounds when evaluator chain disapproves

nested_fields.name: self_critic_instruction
nested_fields.description: Optional extra instruction for built-in 'llm' self-critic evaluator.

nested_fields.name: self_critic_disapprove_feedback
nested_fields.description: Static feedback appended to regeneration notes when evaluator disapproves. Keys are evaluator names; optional '*' applies to any evaluator.

nested_fields.name: use_message_history
nested_fields.description: When True, the LLM step sends a structured message list instead of a flat prompt. System prompt and outer context become the first 'system' message; previous turns from ``context.messages`` are included as-is; the current step prompt is appended as a 'user' message; the LLM response is stored back into ``context.messages`` as an 'assistant' message. Requires a client that supports :meth:`get_response_with_messages` (e.g. OpenAICompatibleClient).

config_fields.name: system_prompt_prefix
config_fields.description: Text prepended before skill instructions in the system prompt

config_fields.name: include_skill_description
config_fields.description: Whether to include the skill description (from frontmatter) in the LLM prompt

config_fields.name: max_instructions_chars
config_fields.description: Maximum characters of skill instructions to include in the LLM system prompt. Skill SKILL.md files can be very large (8-9KB+); truncating prevents ToS rejections from providers that flag large code-heavy prompts. Set to None for no limit.

config_fields.name: strip_code_blocks
config_fields.description: Strip fenced code blocks (```...```) from skill instructions before sending to LLM. Code examples in SKILL.md are guides for the LLM's reasoning, not needed verbatim, and including them can trigger provider ToS filters.

config_fields.name: filter_security_terms
config_fields.description: Remove markdown sections whose headings mention security-sensitive terms (password, encrypt, decrypt) from skill instructions and description. Prevents provider ToS filter rejections caused by security-related content in skill documentation (e.g. PDF decryption instructions).

config_fields.name: script_name
config_fields.description: Relative path to script within skill dir (e.g. 'scripts/extract.py'). Auto-detected if None.

config_fields.name: script_args
config_fields.description: Static CLI args for script execution. Merged with resolved input_mapping values.

config_fields.name: python_executable
config_fields.description: Python interpreter to use for running .py scripts

config_fields.name: working_dir
config_fields.description: Working directory for script execution. Defaults to skill_dir.

config_fields.name: cache_skills
config_fields.description: Cache loaded SkillManifest objects for the lifetime of the process

config_fields.name: skill_cache_dir
config_fields.description: Directory for caching git-cloned or downloaded skills. Defaults to ~/.cache/mmar_carl/skills/

config_fields.name: timeout
config_fields.description: Timeout in seconds for skill execution

config_fields.name: llm_max_iterations
config_fields.description: Maximum number of tool-calling iterations in LLM_AGENT mode. The loop stops when the LLM returns a final response (no tool calls) or this limit is reached.

config_fields.name: persist_workspace
config_fields.description: If True, skip workspace cleanup after LLM_AGENT execution. The workspace path is written to '$memory.agent_skill.<output_memory_key>_workspace' so downstream steps can access files produced without copying them. Only applies to LLM_AGENT mode; other modes do not use a persistent workspace.

config_fields.name: output_capture
config_fields.description: What to capture as the step result. 'stdout' — LLM/script stdout only; 'files' — list of output files from workspace/out; 'both' — stdout plus file paths.

config_fields.name: output_files_glob
config_fields.description: Glob patterns to filter output files collected from workspace/out. Only applies when output_capture is 'files' or 'both'.

config_fields.name: runtime
config_fields.description: Execution runtime for scripts. 'local' — subprocess on host (default, no isolation). 'docker' — requires the Docker CLI/daemon. 'e2b' — requires the mmar-carl[e2b] extra and an API key.

config_fields.name: runtime_config
config_fields.description: Runtime-specific configuration. docker: {'image': 'ghcr.io/...', 'network': 'none', 'mem_limit': '1g'}. e2b:    {'template': 'default', 'api_key_env': 'E2B_API_KEY'}.

config_fields.name: trust_policy
config_fields.description: Controls skill integrity verification. 'any' — no verification (default, suitable for trusted/local skills). 'sha_pinned' — skill_sha256 is required and must match the SKILL.md digest.

config_fields.name: skill_sha256
config_fields.description: Expected SHA256 of the skill's SKILL.md file. Required when trust_policy='sha_pinned'. For GitHub tarballs, this is the hash of the extracted SKILL.md, not the tarball itself.

config_fields.name: extra_pip
config_fields.description: Additional Python packages to install before running skill scripts. Installed into an isolated overlay so the host environment is not modified. Example: ['pdfplumber>=0.11', 'python-pptx>=1.0'].

config_fields.name: output_schema
config_fields.description: Optional JSON-schema-style dict describing the structure of the LLM_AGENT final response. When set, the executor: (1) instructs the agent (in its system context) that the final reply must be JSON matching this schema; (2) parses the final response as JSON; (3) validates the parsed value against the schema. On parse/validation failure the step is marked failed. Only the top-level 'type' (object/array/string/number/integer/boolean/null), 'properties', 'required', and 'items' keys are honoured — this is a lightweight checker, not full JSON Schema. Other modes (LLM/SCRIPT/HYBRID/SUBAGENT) ignore this field.

config_fields.name: output_schema_strict
config_fields.description: When True (default), an unparseable or schema-violating LLM_AGENT final response fails the step. When False, validation failures are logged as warnings on `result_data['schema_warnings']` but the step still succeeds — useful when you want best-effort structured output without blocking the chain.

evaluation.purpose: Inline quality gate: score a prior step's output; can fail/gate downstream.

config_fields.name: evaluates_step
config_fields.description: Step number whose output is evaluated. The evaluation step must declare this step in its dependencies so the output is available in history.

config_fields.name: criteria
config_fields.description: List of evaluation criteria. Interpretation depends on evaluation_method.

config_fields.name: on_fail
config_fields.description: Action to take when one or more criteria are not satisfied.

config_fields.name: evaluation_method
config_fields.description: How to evaluate criteria: 'rule' uses simpleeval expressions, 'llm' uses an LLM judge.

config_fields.name: input_source
config_fields.description: Context reference pointing to the evaluated step's output (e.g. '$history[-1]', '$history[-2]'). Defaults to the most recent history entry.

config_fields.name: max_retries
config_fields.description: Maximum number of LLM retry calls when on_fail=RETRY_WITH_FEEDBACK. After exhausting retries the chain continues normally.

agent_handoff.purpose: Delegate to a complete sub-chain with input/output mapping.

config_fields.name: input_mapping
config_fields.description: Maps resolved parent values to sub-chain memory entries. Keys are 'namespace.key' in sub-chain memory; values are parent context references.

config_fields.name: output_memory_key
config_fields.description: Memory key in the parent context to store the sub-chain's result. Empty string disables automatic result storage.

config_fields.name: output_namespace
config_fields.description: Namespace to use when writing the output to parent memory.

config_fields.name: propagate_failure
config_fields.description: If True, a failed sub-chain marks this step as failed. If False, sub-chain failures are recorded in result_data but the parent step succeeds.

config_fields.name: inherit_tools
config_fields.description: If True, the sub-chain's context receives a copy of the parent tool registry.

config_fields.name: share_memory
config_fields.description: If True, the sub-chain shares the parent context's memory dict *by reference* — writes made by sub-chain steps are visible in the parent after the handoff (collaborating nested chains). If False (default), the sub-chain gets an isolated deep copy and its writes are discarded (only the sub-chain's output flows back via output_memory_key).

config_fields.name: timeout
config_fields.description: Maximum seconds to allow the sub-chain to run. None = no timeout.

parallel_sampling.purpose: Draw N independent LLM samples and aggregate (vote / best-of-N / judge).

config_fields.name: n_samples
config_fields.description: Number of independent LLM samples to draw in parallel.

config_fields.name: aggregation
config_fields.description: Strategy used to select the winning response from all samples.

config_fields.name: judge_prompt
config_fields.description: Optional custom judge prompt for BEST_OF_N / LLM_JUDGE aggregation. Receives the candidates as a numbered list. Leave empty to use the default.

config_fields.name: normalize_for_vote
config_fields.description: Master switch for vote normalisation. When False, samples are compared byte-for-byte and ``vote_normalization`` is ignored. When True (default), ``vote_normalization`` selects the canonicalisation tier.

config_fields.name: vote_normalization
config_fields.description: Canonicalisation tier applied to each sample before counting votes. ``basic`` (default) = ``strip().lower()`` — CARL's historical behaviour. ``aggressive`` also case-folds, collapses internal whitespace and strips surrounding punctuation. Ignored when ``normalize_for_vote`` is False.

config_fields.name: answer_extractor
config_fields.description: Optional callable applied to each raw sample before normalisation and counting, e.g. a numeric or 'final answer:' extractor supplied by a benchmark. Exceptions raised by the extractor are swallowed and the raw sample is used instead. Not serialisable — excluded from ``model_dump``.

config_fields.name: strict
config_fields.description: When True, any silent aggregation fallback (degenerate all-unique vote, unparseable judge reply, judge exception) fails the step instead of returning a first-candidate / vote fallback. Off by default so existing behaviour is unchanged; turn on for experimental runs.

tool_discovery.purpose: Discover and register tools at runtime from a module/callable/dict source.

config_fields.name: source
config_fields.description: Source of tools to discover and register.

config_fields.name: output_memory_key
config_fields.description: If set, writes the list of discovered tool names to ``context.memory['tools'][output_memory_key]`` for downstream inspection.

config_fields.name: tool_timeout
config_fields.description: Optional per-call timeout applied to all discovered sync tools (wraps them with AsyncToolWrapper). Has no effect on async tools.

human_input.purpose: Pause execution and wait for human input (callable or webhook).

config_fields.name: prompt
config_fields.description: Human-readable prompt displayed when asking for input.

config_fields.name: timeout
config_fields.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the typed host callback. Timeout is a non-success outcome. None means wait indefinitely.

config_fields.name: min_length
config_fields.description: Minimum accepted response length.

config_fields.name: max_length
config_fields.description: Maximum accepted response length.

config_fields.name: sensitive
config_fields.description: Redact the answer from StepExecutionResult and model-visible history. Sensitive answers require output_memory_key.

config_fields.name: output_memory_key
config_fields.description: If set, write the collected input to this key in the 'human_input' memory namespace. Useful for downstream steps to read via ``$memory.human_input.<key>``.

supervisor.purpose: LLM routes a task to one of N registered specialist sub-chains.

config_fields.name: routing_prompt
config_fields.description: Prompt template the supervisor LLM sees. Supports ``{task}`` (the resolved task string) and ``{agents}`` (comma-joined agent names).

config_fields.name: task_source
config_fields.description: Where to resolve the task string from. Same syntax as input_mapping values: ``$outer_context``, ``$memory.ns.key``, ``$history[-1]``, or a quoted literal.

config_fields.name: fallback_agent

config_fields.description: Question whose decided value becomes the step result. Defaults to the first question.

config_fields.name: fail_on_uncertain
config_fields.description: Fail the step when an answer is refused or below min_confidence and the question has no fallback. When False the step succeeds and marks the answer uncertain.

config_fields.name: base_url
config_fields.description: Endpoint base URL override (the '/decisions' path is appended). Required for azure_openai, e.g. 'https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/openai/v1'. Must be https except for localhost.

config_fields.name: api_key_env
config_fields.description: Environment variable holding the API key. Defaults to OPENAI_API_KEY, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY by provider.

config_fields.name: timeout
config_fields.description: Per-request timeout in seconds

config_fields.name: max_retries
config_fields.description: Retries on 429, 5xx and network errors (exponential backoff)

config_fields.name: max_state_bytes
config_fields.description: Maximum UTF-8 bytes of the serialized state sent to the provider

config_fields.name: output_memory_key
config_fields.description: Memory key to write {question_name: decided value} to — choice value, predicate bool or score float — so conditional steps can route on it.

config_fields.name: output_namespace
config_fields.description: Memory namespace for output_memory_key

selection.purpose: Select item(s) from a collection by a strategy (top-k / weighted / random / filter / all).

config_fields.name: source
config_fields.description: Reference to the collection to select from (a list resolved from history/memory/metadata).

config_fields.name: strategy
config_fields.description: Selection strategy: 'top_k'/'bottom_k' pick by score, 'weighted' samples proportional to score, 'random' samples uniformly, 'filter' keeps items matching `predicate`, 'all' returns the collection.

config_fields.name: count
config_fields.description: Number of items to select (ignored by 'filter'/'all').

config_fields.name: score_key
config_fields.description: For scored strategies (top_k/bottom_k/weighted): dict key holding each item's numeric score. If None, each item is treated as its own numeric score.

config_fields.name: predicate
config_fields.description: For strategy='filter': a boolean expression (simpleeval) over the bound names `item`/`x`; items where it is truthy are kept.

config_fields.name: seed
config_fields.description: RNG seed for 'weighted'/'random' — set for deterministic selection.

config_fields.name: output_key
config_fields.description: If set, also write the selection to memory under this key.

config_fields.name: namespace
config_fields.description: Memory namespace used when `output_key` is set.

common_fields.name: dependencies
common_fields.description: List of step numbers this step depends on

common_fields.name: triggered_by
common_fields.description: Optional list of event names that gate this step's execution. Used alongside (or instead of) ``dependencies`` for name-based DAG edges. A step becomes ready only when ALL listed events have been emitted via ``context.emit_event(name, payload)`` AND its numeric ``dependencies`` are satisfied. Event payloads can be read via the ``$event.<name>`` reference syntax.

common_fields.name: checkpoint
common_fields.description: Mark this step as a RE-PLAN rollback checkpoint

common_fields.name: replan_enabled
common_fields.description: Optional per-step RE-PLAN override (None = chain policy default)

common_fields.name: frozen
common_fields.description: When True, evolutionary mutation primitives must not alter, retype, or delete this step — lets an evolution engine freeze part of a pipeline and evolve only the rest. Respected by mmar_carl.meta mutation helpers (with respect_frozen=True) and by ChainMutator.

common_fields.name: metrics
common_fields.description: List of MetricBase instances to evaluate after step execution

common_fields.name: metadata
common_fields.description: Free-form step metadata. The executor records provenance here — e.g. a dynamically injected step keeps the number its injector assigned under '__original_injected_number'.

common_fields.name: loop_back_to
common_fields.description: Step number to loop back to after this step completes successfully. Together with loop_config, enables cyclic iteration within the chain. The loop body is the range [loop_back_to, this_step_number] inclusive.

common_fields.name: loop_config
common_fields.description: Loop configuration controlling the loop condition and budget guard. Required when loop_back_to is set.

nested_fields.name: condition_key
nested_fields.description: Reference to the value that controls loop continuation. Accepts any context reference supported by resolve_context_reference: ``$memory.namespace.key``, ``$history[-1]``, or ``$outer_context``. The resolved value is cast to bool; truthy → loop continues. Empty string (default) means 'always loop' up to max_iterations.

nested_fields.name: max_iterations
nested_fields.description: Maximum number of times the loop body may be re-executed (budget guard).

nested_fields.name: negate_condition
nested_fields.description: If True, the continuation decision is negated: loop continues when the resolved value is *falsy* (until-loop semantics). Default False = while-loop semantics.

common_fields.name: cache
common_fields.description: Optional memoization config. When set, the DAGExecutor checks a per-executor in-memory cache before running the step. On a hit the cached result is returned immediately. See StepCache for TTL and custom key_fn options.

nested_fields.name: ttl
nested_fields.description: Cache time-to-live in seconds. After this many seconds the cached result expires and the step will be re-executed on the next call. None (default) means the cache never expires within the current execution.

nested_fields.name: key_fn
nested_fields.description: Optional callable that receives the current ``ReasoningContext`` and returns a string cache key.  When None, the default key combines the step number and the first 256 characters of ``context.outer_context``.

references.description: Output of a previous step by index (negative allowed); bare form is the whole list.
Read namespaced shared memory. Namespace defaults to 'default' when omitted.
Read long-term memory (requires an LTMBase backend wired into the context).
Most-recent payload emitted for an event via context.emit_event(name, payload).
Structured per-step metadata stored under context.metadata['step_results'][N]. Declare step N as a direct or transitive dependency of every consumer.
The chain's original input. Parsed as JSON when it looks like JSON, else the raw string.
A quoted string literal, passed through verbatim (outer quotes stripped).
Fallback: an unprefixed key is looked up in context.metadata.

validation_rules.rule: A chain must contain at least one step.
Each step.number must be unique within the chain.
Every value in step.dependencies must reference an existing step.number.
The dependency graph must be acyclic (no cycles).
A catalogued $steps.N read must name an existing direct or transitive dependency.
step_type must be one of the registered StepType values.
Each step must provide the required fields for its step_type (see the catalog card).
A $memory.ns.key read should be written by a prior step or pre-populated before execution.
A $history[N] read with N >= the history depth at that point resolves to None.
